data.name: EventSourceClassMustNotBeAbstractTitle
data.value: An event source class must not be an abstract class

data.name: EventSourceClassMustNotBeAbstractMessage
data.value: The event source class '{0}' is declared abstract

data.name: EventSourceClassMustNotBeAbstractDescription
data.value: EventSource is designed around a concrete type: the event manifest is derived from the members of the type that is instantiated, and the generated event writing methods are instance members that call protected members of EventSource. An abstract class can never be instantiated, so nothing it declares would ever write an event. Either remove the abstract modifier, or move GeneratedEventSourceAttribute to the concrete class that is actually instantiated. To share members across several event sources, declare the abstract base class without GeneratedEventSourceAttribute and apply the attribute only to the leaf concrete classes. Do not suppress this diagnostic; an abstract event source can never emit events.

data.name: EventSourceClassMustDeriveFromEventSourceTitle
data.value: An event source class must derive from System.Diagnostics.Tracing.EventSource

data.name: EventSourceClassMustDeriveFromEventSourceMessage
data.value: The event source class '{0}' does not derive from System.Diagnostics.Tracing.EventSource

data.name: EventSourceClassMustDeriveFromEventSourceDescription
data.value: The generated method bodies call WriteEvent and WriteEventCore, which are protected members of System.Diagnostics.Tracing.EventSource, so they only compile inside a type that inherits them. Add System.Diagnostics.Tracing.EventSource, or a class derived from it, to the base class list of the event source class; the base class list may appear on any partial part. If the class is not meant to be an event source, remove GeneratedEventSourceAttribute instead. Do not suppress this diagnostic; suppressing it moves the failure into the generated file, where the errors point at code you cannot edit.

data.name: EventSourceClassMustBePartialClassTitle
data.value: An event source class must be a partial class

data.name: EventSourceClassMustBePartialClassMessage
data.value: The type '{0}' is not declared partial

data.name: EventSourceClassMustBePartialClassDescription
data.value: The source generator writes the bodies of the event writing methods into a separate file, as an additional part of the event source class. A type can be split across several files only when every declaration involved is declared partial, and that applies to the whole containing chain: if the event source class is nested, each enclosing type must be partial as well. Add the partial modifier to the type named in the message, which is not necessarily the event source class itself. Do not suppress this diagnostic; suppressing it does not make the generator emit anything, and the declared partial methods stay unimplemented.

data.name: EventSourceClassMustNotBeFileLocalClassTitle
data.value: An event source class must not be a file-local class

data.name: EventSourceClassMustNotBeFileLocalClassMessage
data.value: The type '{0}' is declared as a file-local type

data.name: EventSourceClassMustNotBeFileLocalClassDescription
data.value: A file-local type has a distinct identity in every file that declares it, because the compiler mangles its metadata name with a per-file component. A partial part contributed from another file therefore declares an unrelated type instead of completing this one, which makes the type impossible for the generator to augment no matter how many partial modifiers are present. Remove the file modifier from the type named in the message; if the type must stay invisible outside its file, internal is the closest alternative the generator can work with. Do not suppress this diagnostic; unlike a missing partial modifier, this failure produces no compiler error that names the cause.

data.name: EventSourceNestedTypeVisibilityJustification
data.value: EventSource discovers the Keywords, Tasks, and Opcodes values only in public nested classes with those exact names, so nesting and their public accessibility are required, not accidental design choices.

data.name: ParameterTypeNotSupportedTitle
data.value: An event method parameter must have a supported type

data.name: ParameterTypeNotSupportedMessage
data.value: The type '{1}' of the parameter '{0}' is not supported

data.name: ParameterTypeNotSupportedDescription
data.value: EventSource writes event payloads as a flat sequence of fixed-layout fields, so a parameter can only be included in the payload when its type has a size EventSource recognizes. The supported parameter types are bool, byte, char, DateTime, decimal, double, short, int, long, nint, sbyte, float, string, ushort, uint, ulong, Guid, byte[], and any enum type. Change the parameter to one of these types, converting at the call site rather than inside the event method so the conversion does not run when nobody is listening to the event source. Do not suppress this diagnostic; the parameter cannot be written to the payload, so the generated method would either fail to compile or silently drop the value.
